dominant_medium: Lomekwian knapped basalt cores & anvils
source: Harmand et al. (2015) Nature 521:310; Stout et al. (2015) PLoS ONE 10:e0121804
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: non-symbolic lithic templates (~10-30 bits of platform/strike geometry per tool type across small Pliocene hominin populations; 10^2-10^4 bits).

dominant_medium: Oldowan flaked stone cores & chopper debitage
source: Semaw et al. (2003) J. Hum. Evol. 45:169; Braun et al. (2019) PNAS 116:11712; Toth & Schick (2009) Annu. Rev. Anthropol. 38:289
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: culturally transmitted Oldowan core-reduction sequences across African hominin bands (~10^3-10^5 bits).

dominant_medium: Acheulean 3D bilaterally symmetric stone handaxes (bifaces)
source: Beyene et al. (2013) PNAS 110:1584; Lepre et al. (2011) Nature 477:82; Stout et al. (2015) PLoS ONE 10:e0121804
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: standardized 3D Acheulean bifaces across Africa and Eurasia (~10^4-10^6 bits of persistent morphological manufacture templates).

dominant_medium: Levallois prepared-core lithics, hafted tools & wooden spears
source: Thieme (1997) Nature 385:807; Adler et al. (2014) Science 345:1609; Mazza et al. (2006) J. Quaternary Sci. 21:601
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: hierarchical multi-step Levallois reduction, birch-pitch hafting recipes, and wooden weaponry (~10^5-2x10^6 bits).

dominant_medium: Middle Stone Age prepared-core blades & ground red-ochre pigments
source: Hublin et al. (2017) Nature 546:289; Brooks et al. (2018) Science 360:90
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: pan-African Middle Stone Age toolkits and processed mineral pigments (~3x10^5-5x10^6 bits).

dominant_medium: Engraved red-ochre plaques, engraved ostrich eggshells & perforated shell beads
source: Henshilwood et al. (2002) Science 295:1278; Henshilwood et al. (2009) J. Hum. Evol. 57:27; Texier et al. (2010) PNAS 107:6180; d'Errico et al. (2005) J. Hum. Evol. 48:3
note: First unambiguous symbolic engravings (Blombos cross-hatched ochre, Diepkloof eggshells) and Nassarius beads; total global stock across ~20,000-40,000 bands is an order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate (~10^6-5x10^7 bits).

dominant_medium: Upper Paleolithic parietal cave paintings, portable ivory carvings & notched bone tallies
source: Oktaviana et al. (2024) Nature 631:814; Aubert et al. (2019) Nature 576:442; Valladas et al. (2001) Nature 413:479; d'Errico et al. (2018) PNAS 115:9964
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: figurative and geometric rock art from Sulawesi (>45.5-51.2 ka) to Chauvet plus incised bone tallies (~10^7-5x10^8 bits).

dominant_medium: Megalithic stone reliefs (Göbekli Tepe) & plain Neolithic clay accounting tokens
source: Dietrich et al. (2012) Antiquity 86:674; Schmandt-Besserat (1992) Before Writing, Univ. Texas Press
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: carved T-pillar iconography and geometric clay counting tokens across early Near Eastern farming villages (~5x10^7-10^9 bits).

dominant_medium: Clay accounting envelopes (bullae), complex tokens & cylinder/stamp seals
source: Schmandt-Besserat (1992) Before Writing, Univ. Texas Press; Pittman (1994) The Glazed Steatite Glyptic Style; Nissen, Damerow & Englund (1993) Archaic Bookkeeping
note: Order-of-magnitude archaeological estimate: tens of thousands of Chalcolithic temple-town sealings and token-filled bullae (~3x10^8-3x10^9 bits).

dominant_medium: Early Bronze Age proto-cuneiform clay tablets & Early Dynastic Egyptian inscriptions/papyri
source: Nissen, Damerow & Englund (1993) Archaic Bookkeeping, Univ. Chicago Press; Streck (2010) Mitt. Dtsch. Orient-Ges. 142:35; Regulski (2016) Oxford Handbooks
note: ~5,000 Uruk IV-III proto-cuneiform tablets survive today (~2x10^6 bits excavated from Uruk alone); Streck (2010) counts >500,000 total excavated cuneiform tablets (~14M+ evaluated words ~5x10^8 bits surviving across all Bronze/Iron Age periods). Accounting for <1-5% archaeological survival plus Egyptian papyri/labels yields ~2x10^9-10^10 active bits c. 3000 BCE.

dominant_medium: Cuneiform palace/temple archives, Egyptian papyrus rolls, Shang oracle bones & early alphabets
source: Streck (2010) Mitt. Dtsch. Orient-Ges. 142:35; Keightley (1978) Sources of Shang History, Univ. Calif. Press; Beckman (1999) Hittite Diplomatic Texts; Goldwasser (2010) Bibl. Archaeol. Rev. 36:36
note: ~150,000 excavated Anyang oracle-bone fragments (Keightley 1978), ~30,000 Hattusa tablets, Amarna/Ugarit archives, and New Kingdom papyri represent the surviving tip of several million active Late Bronze Age records (~10^10-5x10^10 bits).

dominant_medium: Papyrus scrolls, Zhou bamboo/wooden slip bundles, Achaemenid clay archives & inscriptions
source: Streck (2010) Mitt. Dtsch. Orient-Ges. 142:35; Tsien (1985) Paper and Printing (Needham Vol. 5 Pt. 1), Cambridge Univ. Press; Henkelman (2008) The Other Gods Who Are (Persepolis Fortification Archive)
note: Persepolis Fortification Archive alone yielded ~20,000-30,000 Elamite/Aramaic tablets; across Greek/Egyptian papyrus rolls, Indian grammatical/administrative records, and Warring States bamboo slips, global stock ~5x10^10-1.5x10^11 bits (census 5.0e10 sits within range).

dominant_medium: Hellenistic papyrus scroll libraries (Alexandria/Pergamon) & Qin/Han bamboo-slip and silk archives
source: Bagnall (2002) Proc. Am. Philos. Soc. 146:348; Ban Gu (c. 82 CE) Hanshu Yiwenzhi; Tsien (1985) Paper and Printing, Cambridge Univ. Press; Wilkinson (2022) Chinese History: A New Manual
note: Bagnall (2002) critiques legendary 400,000-700,000 scroll counts for Alexandria and estimates ~40,000-100,000 rolls (~3x10^10-10^11 bits in Alexandria alone at ~0.5-1 Mb/scroll); the Han imperial catalog Hanshu Yiwenzhi listed 13,269 scrolls (juan) across 596 works (~10^10 bits in one palace collection). Across all Mediterranean, Persian, Indian, and Chinese libraries/registries, global stock ~1x10^11-5x10^11 bits (census 1.0e11 sits at the lower bound).

dominant_medium: Parchment (vellum) bound codices, Chinese paper scrolls & Indian palm-leaf manuscripts
source: Buringh & van Zanden (2009) J. Econ. Hist. 69:409; Roberts & Skeat (1983) The Birth of the Codex, Oxford Univ. Press; Tsien (1985) Paper and Printing
note: Buringh & van Zanden (2009) Table 1 shows Western European manuscript output collapsed to 13,551/century by the 6th c., while Eastern Roman/Byzantine, Sasanian, Gupta Indian, and Chinese paper archives (Suishu Jingjizhi c. 600 CE recorded 36,708-89,666 imperial scrolls alone) sustained ~2-4x10^5 volumes globally (~2x10^11-4x10^11 bits; census 2.0e11 agrees).

dominant_medium: Abbasid/Fatimid/Córdoba rag-paper codices, Song woodblock-printed books & Latin vellum manuscripts
source: Buringh & van Zanden (2009) J. Econ. Hist. 69:409; Bloom (2001) Paper Before Print, Yale Univ. Press; Tsien (1985) Paper and Printing, Cambridge Univ. Press
note: Buringh & van Zanden (2009) Table 1 records 347,667 Western European manuscripts across the 10th-11th centuries, dwarfed c. 1000 CE by Islamic rag-paper libraries (Baghdad, Cairo, Córdoba) and Northern Song woodblock printing (130,000-block Tripitaka and 1,000-juan imperial encyclopedias): ~0.6-1.5M global volumes x ~1 Mb ~ 6x10^11-1.5x10^12 bits (census 5.0e11 sits just below central estimate).

dominant_medium: Late-medieval paper/vellum manuscripts, Ming/Korean woodblock & metal-type imprints, and first Gutenberg incunabula
source: Buringh & van Zanden (2009) J. Econ. Hist. 69:409; Tsien (1985) Paper and Printing; Brokaw & Chow (2005) Printing and Book Culture in Late Imperial China, Univ. Calif. Press
note: DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (4x low in census): Buringh & van Zanden (2009) Table 1 records 2,746,951 European manuscripts in the 14th c. and 4,999,160 in the 15th c. (~4,996,573 produced 1300-1450, plus 12,587,000 printed incunabula in 1454-1500), alongside Ming China woodblock publishing (Yongle Encyclopedia 1408 = 22,937 juan / 370M characters). ~4-6M extant Eurasian volumes in 1450 x ~1.5-2 Mb/book = ~8x10^12 bits (vs census 2.0e12).

dominant_medium: Early modern printed books, copperplate atlases, logarithmic tables & scientific journals
source: Buringh & van Zanden (2009) J. Econ. Hist. 69:409 (Table 2); Brokaw & Chow (2005) Printing and Book Culture in Late Imperial China
note: MAJOR DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (50x low in census): Summing Buringh & van Zanden (2009) Table 2 from 1454 to 1665 gives 530,400,000 printed books produced in Europe alone (~200-300M extant after loss/wear, plus ~50-100M Ming/Qing and Islamic volumes). ~2.5-3.0x10^8 extant books x ~1.5-2.0x10^6 bits/book = ~5.0x10^14 bits (500 terabits), whereas census 1.0e13 bits implied only ~5M books!

dominant_medium: Steam-press printed books & newspapers, parish/state civil registries, Jacquard cards & early daguerreotypes
source: Buringh & van Zanden (2009) J. Econ. Hist. 69:409 (Table 2); Eliot (1994) Some Patterns and Trends in British Publishing 1800-1919; Hilbert & López (2011) Science 332:60
note: DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (10x low in census): Buringh & van Zanden (2009) Table 2 already totals 1,759,755,000 European printed books in 1454-1800, and Koenig steam cylinder presses (from 1814) accelerated output through 1844 (~1.5-2B extant global books + newspapers/archives x ~1.5-2 Mb = ~3.0x10^15 bits vs census 3.0e14).

dominant_medium: Rotary-press wood-pulp books & daily newspapers, photographic plates, phonograph cylinders & Hollerith punch cards
source: Eliot (1994) Some Patterns and Trends in British Publishing 1800-1919; Weedon (2003) Victorian Publishing; Austrian (1982) Herman Hollerith; Hilbert & López (2011) Science 332:60
note: DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (13x low in census): Cheap wood-pulp rotary presses, national library/patent/census archives (62M US 1890 Hollerith cards), and silver-halide photography plates pushed global analog storage to ~2x10^16 bits (vs census 1.5e15).

dominant_medium: Mass print libraries, 35mm cinema & aerial-reconnaissance film, microfilm & shellac audio discs
source: Hilbert & López (2011) Science 332:60 (Supporting Online Appendix analog baselines); Lyman & Varian (2003) How Much Information
note: DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (35x low in census): Analog cinema/photographic film (~10^7-10^8 bits/frame), microfilm, and mass print dominated 20th-century storage long before digital disks—reaching 2.08e+19 compressed bits (99.2% analog) by 1986 (Hilbert & López 2011). Back-projecting 1945 film + print stock gives ~7x10^17 bits (vs census 2.0e16).

dominant_medium: Global analog print, photographic/cinema film, vinyl & broadcast tape, plus mainframe magnetic tape/disks
source: Hilbert & López (2011) Science 332:60; Phister (1979) Data Processing Technology and Economics, Digital Press
note: DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (40x low in census): In 1986, Hilbert & López (2011) measured 2.6 EB = 2.08e+19 optimally compressed bits, still 99.2% analog (video/audio tape, photo/cinema film, paper). Census 1.0e17 bits in 1965 counted early mainframe/instrumentation tape + core, omitting ~4x10^18 bits (~0.5 EB) of global analog film, broadcast tape, and print.

dominant_medium: Analog videotape, paper & film (75%) + digital magnetic HDDs, optical CD/DVDs & tape (25%)
note: MAJOR 10x EXPONENT TYPO IN CENSUS FLAGGED: Hilbert & López (2011) measured 2000 global storage at 54.5 exabytes (optimally compressed, ~12 CD-ROMs/person) = 5.45x10^19 BYTES x 8 bits/byte = 4.36e+20 bits (~4.4x10^20 bits). Census 4.4e19 dropped one factor of 10 (and the source register entry for Hilbert & López similarly confused 2007's 2.95x10^20 bytes with bits; 295 EB in 2007 = 2.36e+21 bits).

dominant_medium: Enterprise & consumer magnetic HDDs, early smartphone/SSD NAND flash & LTO magnetic tape
source: Hilbert & López (2011) Science 332:60 (2007 anchor: 295 EB = 2.36x10^21 bits); Gantz & Reinsel (2010, 2012) IDC Digital Universe; Rydning (2018) IDC StorageSphere
note: FLOW-VS-STOCK NOTE: Hilbert & López (2011) give 2.36x10^21 bits (295 EB) in 2007; IDC installed raw storage capacity in 2010 was ~700 EB = 5.6x10^21 bits, whereas census 9.6e21 bits (1.2 ZB) copied IDC's 2010 annual Digital Universe data-creation flow (1.2 ZB/yr) rather than installed storage capacity.

dominant_medium: Cloud PMR magnetic hard disks, MLC NAND flash SSDs, mobile flash & LTO archival tape
source: Gantz & Reinsel (2012) IDC Digital Universe in 2020; Rydning (2018, 2021) IDC Worldwide Global StorageSphere
note: IDC installed storage base in 2012 reached ~1.3-2.0 ZB (~1.0x10^22-1.6x10^22 bits, vs 2.8 ZB/yr annual Digital Universe flow); 1.2e22 bits (1.5 ZB) sits smoothly on the ~21%/yr trajectory from 2007 (2.36e21) to 2020 (5.36e22), and census 1.6e22 (2.0 ZB) is within 33%.

dominant_medium: 3D TLC NAND flash SSDs, helium PMR cloud HDDs & enterprise LTO magnetic tape
source: Rydning (2021) IDC Worldwide Global StorageSphere Forecast, 2021-2025 (Doc #US47509621)
note: IDC StorageSphere measured the 2020 global installed storage base at 6.7 ZB = 5.36e+22 bits (~5.4e22 bits); census numeric value 5.0e22 bits (6.25 ZB) agrees within 7%, though the 2020 text description ('~5x10^23 bits / 64 ZB') cited annual DataSphere traffic (64.2 ZB/yr) instead of installed StorageSphere (6.7 ZB).

dominant_medium: 3D TLC/QLC NAND flash SSDs, PMR/HAMR cloud HDDs, LTO-9/10 magnetic tape & optical archives
source: Rydning (2024, 2025) IDC Worldwide Global StorageSphere Forecast; INSIC Magnetic Tape Roadmap (2025)
note: Kept at canonical 1.2e23 bits (15.0 ZB installed storage base across ~54e21b HDD + ~48e21b NAND SSD + ~18e21b tape/optical; strictly separated from ~200 ZB/yr annual IP/DataSphere flow).
